correctness.rationale: At a nonobtuse vertex of a parallelogram, adjacent side vectors have nonnegative dot product. Squared distance from that vertex is strictly increasing along each of the two boundary chains to the opposite vertex, because the only nontrivial derivatives are 2 a·b + 2 t|b|^2 and 2 a·b + 2 t|a|^2. Thus any centered circle meets each chain at most once. Every boundary point of a nondegenerate polygon has a sufficiently small centered circle with two boundary intersections, giving the reverse inequality. The package checker independently verifies the derivative algebra and critical-radius intersection sweeps.

value.rationale: Parallelograms are exactly the centrally symmetric convex quadrilaterals and form a canonical Euclidean family spanning all aspect ratios and shears. The invariant is not affine-invariant, so this is not a square renaming. The theorem restores Erdős's original sharp constant 2 on a full natural class and strictly improves the known general quadrilateral upper bound 4.
